items.title: Fix useCountryConfig EU site resolution
items.tldr: While scoping the EU language mismatch story I found useCountryConfig silently returns the Australian config on all four EU Domestic storefronts, and its test hides this by mocking a site ID the config can never produce. A new session would fix the comparison, correct the test, and clean up a misleading comment in the footer that repeats the same wrong assumption.
items.prompt:
Fix a latent site-resolution bug in `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` in the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa).

THE BUG
`useCountryConfig()` resolves the active region with:

    const match = Object.values(COUNTRIES).find((c) => c.sfccSiteId === site?.id && c.locale === locale?.id);

`site` comes from the base SFCC `useMultiSite()`, whose site object is built by `config/sites.js`. That file emits `{ id, sfccSiteId?, l10n }` — `id` is the **PWA site id** and `sfccSiteId` is a **separate field**, present only on the four EU Domestic sites:

    { id: 'ZimmermannEUen', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'en-GB', alias: 'en-eu' }] },
    { id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'fr',    alias: 'fr-eu' }] },
    { id: 'ZimmermannEUit', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'it',    alias: 'it-eu' }] },
    { id: 'ZimmermannEUes', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU', locales: [{ id: 'es',    alias: 'es-eu' }] },

`overrides/app/config/countries.generated.ts` gives all four EU slugs `sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU'`. So the comparison is `'ZimmermannEU' === 'ZimmermannEUfr'` → false on every EU Domestic site, and the hook falls through to `COUNTRIES[DEFAULT_COUNTRY_SLUG]` (AU) — wrong currency, wrong checkoutOwner, wrong globalEPricing. Every other storefront works, because those sites have no `sfccSiteId` override so `id` and `sfccSiteId` coincide.

WHY IT'S NOT CAUGHT
`overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.test.ts` has a `mockSite(siteId, localeId)` helper that sets `{ site: { id: siteId } }`, and the four EU tests pass `'ZimmermannEU'` as that id — a value `config/sites.js` can never emit. The tests pass while the runtime path fails.

SCOPE OF WORK
1. Fix the comparison in `useCountryConfig.ts` to prefer the explicit SFCC id and fall back to the PWA id, e.g. `c.sfccSiteId === (site?.sfccSiteId ?? site?.id)`. Widen the local `MultiSiteContext` type to include `sfccSiteId?: string` on `site`.
2. Fix the test: `mockSite` should set a realistic site object (`{ id: 'ZimmermannEUfr', sfccSiteId: 'ZimmermannEU' }`) for the EU cases, so the suite exercises what `config/sites.js` actually produces. **Make the corrected test fail against the current implementation first, to prove it covers the bug**, then apply the fix.
3. Fix the misleading comment in `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` (~line 194-196). It claims `site.id` "is the resolved SFCC site ID — confirmed against useCountryConfig.ts's identical client-side pattern". That is wrong: `site.id` is the PWA site id. The footer's own behaviour is CORRECT and must not change — it passes `site.id` into `pickMostSpecificByRegion`, and `scripts/contentful/setup/seedRegions.mjs` seeds Contentful `region.siteId` with PWA site ids (`ZimmermannEUen`/`EUfr`/`EUit`/`EUes`/`EUIntl`), so they match. Only correct the comment so it stops propagating the wrong belief.

CONSTRAINTS
- `overrides/` is TypeScript only. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run test` before finishing.
- Do NOT modify `config/` or `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` / `countries.generated.ts` — `config/` is Tier 1 absolute and `countries.ts` is Tier 1 (see `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`). The fix belongs entirely in the hook, its test, and the footer comment.
- `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` is Tier 4 (unlisted); `overrides/app/components/footer/` is Tier 2 (Global Shell, both squads) — a comment-only change there is fine but note it in the PR.
- Start from a new branch off `develop` (`fix/usecountryconfig-eu-site-resolution`). Do not commit or push without being asked.

items.title: Restore promo code entry on checkout payment step
items.tldr: While investigating checkout order-summary errors for a design alignment, found that Zimmermann's Adyen payment.tsx override silently dropped the base PromoCode component — checkout can currently only remove an existing coupon, never apply a new one. This session would restore entry per the signed-off CFD-017/PRC-27 requirement.
items.prompt:
Checkout's promo/coupon entry is currently broken: a customer can remove an already-applied coupon at checkout, but cannot apply a new one.

Root cause: base Salesforce `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.jsx` imports and renders the shared `PromoCode` component (`import {PromoCode, usePromoCode} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/promo-code'` at line 38, `usePromoCode()` hook at line 91, `<PromoCode {...promoCodeProps} itemProps={{border: 'none'}} />` at line 183). Zimmermann's override at `overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/payment.tsx` (added for Adyen integration) has zero references to promo/PromoCode anywhere — the component was dropped entirely, apparently as an unintentional casualty of the Adyen work rather than a deliberate design decision.

This regresses a signed-off requirement: `.docs/prd/checkout.md` CFD-017 ("Promo code field with success and error states") and `.docs/prd/promotions.md` PRC-27/PRC-29. Jira story [SFCC-331](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-331) ("Checkout – Promo Code Entry & Validation") explicitly describes this field living in checkout's right-hand order summary panel — so promo entry at checkout is confirmed in-scope, not something intentionally removed.

Note: `overrides/app/components/promo-code/` does not exist yet as an override — the live component today is the unmodified base at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/promo-code/index.jsx`. Follow this repo's AGENTS.md Copy-first rule (see `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` and AGENTS.md's "Coding Task Workflow") if creating that override becomes necessary as part of the fix, rather than just re-wiring the base import back into `payment.tsx`. Confirm with the current codebase state before assuming anything above is still accurate — this was found in a design-alignment investigation, not a fix session, so nothing has changed yet.

items.title: Reconcile stale mega-menu docs with Contentful-only build
items.tldr: While investigating how the mega menu works, found that the team already decided (and shipped) a full-Contentful nav replacement back in late August 2026, rejecting the BM-category-tree/hybrid model the original tickets specified — but the confirmed integration doc and project memory were never updated to say so. This session will bring the docs and a couple of stale code comments in line with what's actually built.
items.prompt:
Context: Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa). An investigation into the mega menu / global nav confirmed the following as-built architecture: the desktop mega menu (`overrides/app/components/list-menu/`) and mobile drawer nav (`overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/`) both fetch their data exclusively from Contentful via `overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts` (content type `headerNavigation` → `headerNavItem[]` → `navGroup`/`link`, with `link.href` a free-text string). The SFCC category tree that `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` still fetches via `useCategory()` and passes down as `root`/`itemsKey`/`itemsCountKey` props is explicitly ignored by both components — confirmed directly by reading `list-menu/list-menu.tsx:148-168`, whose own `ListMenuProps` JSDoc says those props are "accepted only for call-site compatibility with base `_app.jsx`'s SFCC category-tree contract... all of these are ignored except `maxColumns`."

This was a deliberate decision: a planning session log at `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md` (~lines 1041-1047) shows the original tickets (SFCC-96, SFCC-746, SFCC-28) specified a BM-category-tree-driven or hybrid model, and the team explicitly rejected that in favour of "full Contentful replacement everywhere, including subcategory links" during planning.

The problem: the confirmed documentation was never updated to reflect this decision, so it actively misleads anyone who reads it instead of the code:

1. **`.docs/integration/02-contentful.md`** — §1's content-ownership table (around line 33) lists `Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | Pending`. This should be updated to reflect that Contentful owns the entire nav tree (labels, links, columns, images), not just promotional tiles, and that this is settled, not Pending. §10's open item #2 (around lines 133-136) makes the same "Pending... working assumption is in the ownership table" statement and should be resolved/removed or rewritten to record the actual decision and cite `.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md` as the source.

2. **`.docs/temp/openItems.md`** (around lines 51-53) — repeats the same stale "SFCC category tree + Contentful promo tiles" framing. Update or remove this item to match.

3. **`.docs/memory/projectState.md`** (last updated 2026-08-24) — doesn't mention the SFCC-52/746/96/97 mega-menu/nav work at all despite it running through 2026-08-31. Add an entry recording that the header/mega-menu/drawer nav is built and Contentful-driven (per this investigation). Also check its existing line noting "the mobile hamburger drawer has zero category navigation links" (around lines 79-82, under an SFCC-751 entry) — this is very likely superseded by the drawer nav build (`drawer-menu/index.tsx` now drills L1→L2 using Contentful-sourced items) and should be confirmed/retracted if so, rather than left contradicting the newer work.

4. **Stale code comments** — three files still say the mega-menu/drawer "isn't wired to any real state," dated to commit `ee9f1f23` (2026-08-27), but the wiring landed in the very next commits on the same branch (SFCC-96 commits `d9a064bb7`/`2b42527ab`, SFCC-97 commits `a2a687ae5`/`82f12cb6`): `overrides/app/components/header/headerTypes.ts:17-21`, `overrides/app/components/header/leftBar/index.tsx:16-19,21-22`, `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx:133-138,140-141`. Update these comments to reflect that `header/index.tsx` now derives and passes a real `menuExpanded` value (see `header/index.tsx:164-211`).

5. **`scripts/contentful/content-types/headerNavItem.js:29-31`** — comment claims `navGroup` "is authored on a separate branch... and has no local file in this content-types/ directory yet." This is false now — `navGroup.js` exists in the same directory (it was merged, unifying the old `footerNavGroup` type). Fix the comment.

Notes on file tiers (per `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`): the `.docs/` files are not tier-classified at all, safe to edit directly. `scripts/contentful/content-types/` is Tier 2 (owner: Integration/SI Partner — notify before changing), but this is a comment-only fix with no schema/behavior change. The three header component files are Tier 2 "Global Shell" (owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching), also comment-only. Follow this repo's AGENTS.md workflow (clarify → plan → implement) and its Doc integrity rule — since `.docs/integration/02-contentful.md` is a confirmed integration doc, treat correcting it as flagging-and-fixing a doc/reality conflict per that rule, not a silent edit; a short note in the PR description calling out what changed and why (citing this investigation) is appropriate.

items.title: Confirm and remove dead SFCC category fetch in _app
items.tldr: Investigating the mega menu turned up that `_app/index.tsx` still fetches the SFCC category tree and hands it to ListMenu/DrawerMenu, but both components now explicitly ignore that data (they self-fetch nav from Contentful instead) — so the fetch, and the two `withCommerceSdkReact`-wrapped helper components built for it, look like dead code. This is Tier 2 shared-shell code both squads touch, so it needs a careful confirm-then-remove pass, not a drive-by delete.
items.prompt:
Context: Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit (/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa). While investigating how the mega menu / global nav works, found that `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` does the following, apparently for nothing:

- Lines 161-164: `const { data: categoriesTree } = useCategory({ parameters: { id: CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY, levels: CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_NAV_SSR_DEPTH } }); const categories = flatten((categoriesTree || {}) as CategoryNode, 'categories');` — an SFCC category-tree fetch via commerce-sdk-react.
- Lines 121-158: two `withCommerceSdkReact`-wrapped components, `DrawerMenuItemWithData` and `ListMenuContentWithData`, built specifically to lazily fetch sub-category data per nav item as it's expanded.
- Lines 428-445: `categories` is passed as `root`/`itemsKey="categories"`/`itemsCountKey="onlineSubCategoriesCount"` to `<DrawerMenu>`, and the two `WithData` helper components are passed as `itemComponent`/`contentComponent`.

This mirrors the base, un-overridden SFCC `_app.jsx` template's contract exactly — but the Zimmermann overrides of both consumers ignore it. Confirmed directly: `overrides/app/components/list-menu/list-menu.tsx:148-168` — its `ListMenuProps` type has a JSDoc comment stating `root`/`contentComponent`/`itemsKey`/`itemsCountKey` are "accepted only for call-site compatibility with base `_app.jsx`'s SFCC category-tree contract. `ListMenu` self-fetches its own data via `useHeaderNav()`, so all of these are ignored except `maxColumns`." The container function (lines 164-168) only destructures `maxColumns` and calls `useHeaderNav()` — it never reads `root` at all. `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.tsx` appears (per a research trace, not yet independently re-verified line-by-line) to follow the identical pattern for `DrawerMenu`.

The ask: verify this precisely — read `drawer-menu/index.tsx`'s container function the same way `list-menu.tsx`'s was verified above, and confirm neither `root`, `itemsKey`, `itemsCountKey`, `itemComponent`, nor `contentComponent` is actually read for rendering in either component (as opposed to being destructured-but-unused, which would still mean dead code, vs. actually consumed somewhere non-obvious). Also check whether `categories`/`categoriesTree` from `_app/index.tsx:161-164` is used ANYWHERE else in that file or passed to any other consumer besides the two nav components — the investigation that found this did not rule that out with certainty. If truly unused everywhere:

1. Remove the `useCategory` call, the `categories`/`flatten` derivation, and the `DrawerMenuItemWithData`/`ListMenuContentWithData` component definitions from `_app/index.tsx`.
2. Remove the `root`/`itemsKey`/`itemsCountKey`/`itemComponent` props passed to `<DrawerMenu>` and the `root`/`itemsKey`/`itemsCountKey`/`contentComponent` props passed to `<ListMenu>`.
3. Once those props are gone from the call site, `ListMenuProps`/`DrawerMenu`'s equivalent prop type can likely drop the now-fully-unused `root`/`itemsKey`/`itemsCountKey`/`itemComponent`/`contentComponent` fields entirely too (check `drawer-menu`'s prop type name) — but confirm nothing else references those prop names first (e.g. a story or test file constructing one of these components with those props).
4. Check whether `flatten` (from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils`) and `CategoryNode`/`CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY`/`CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_NAV_SSR_DEPTH` imports become unused as a result and remove them too.

This is `overrides/app/components/_app/` — Tier 2 "Global Shell" per `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` (owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching), so per this repo's AGENTS.md rules, treat this as a single-tier, minimal-scope change (Hard Rule 5: never refactor upward — don't touch anything in `list-menu`/`drawer-menu` themselves, only `_app/index.tsx`), run `npx tsc --noEmit` after, and call out in the PR description that this removes now-dead code surfaced by a mega-menu architecture investigation (cite the investigation, not a re-derivation of "why" in code comments — AGENTS.md prefers no comments explaining removed code, just clean removal). If it turns out `categories`/`categoriesTree` IS used elsewhere in `_app/index.tsx` that the original investigation missed, stop and report that instead of partially removing it.

items.title: Register /social-callback route in overrides/app/routes.tsx
items.tldr: While scoping checkout social login I found the IDP redirect-back route is never registered, because the overrides router only pulls in the base static route list and skips the part that adds it. Social sign-in is enabled on every tier today, so a returning shopper likely lands on the catch-all instead of the auth handler.
items.prompt:
Investigate and fix a route-registration gap for social login in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa.

PROBLEM
`overrides/app/routes.tsx:15` imports ONLY the named static export from base:
  `import { routes as _routes } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes';`

But the base package registers the social-login callback route, the passwordless landing route and the reset-password landing route in its DEFAULT export function, not in that static array — see `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx:131-166`, specifically lines 153-157:

    socialLoginEnabled &&
        socialRedirectURI && {
            path: socialRedirectURI,
            component: SocialLoginRedirect,
            exact: true
        }

`overrides/app/routes.tsx` never calls that default export — it builds its own array and calls `configureRoutes` itself. Result: `/social-callback` (config/default.js:109), `/passwordless-login-landing` (config/default.js:97) and `/reset-password-landing` (config/default.js:118) appear to have no React route at all.

CORROBORATING EVIDENCE
- `.claude/registry/routes.md` (generated 2026-09-23 from overrides/app/routes.tsx + inherited base routes) lists none of those three paths.
- `overrides/app/ssr.js:115` DOES allowlist `^/social-callback` in the CDN/WAF rule, so the path was expected to exist.
- Social login is enabled on every named tier: config/dev.js:15-18, config/sit.js:15-18, config/test.js, config/uat.js, config/staging.js, config/production.js:15-18, plus pr-* preview targets via `IS_PREVIEW_TARGET` (config/default.js:39, 102).
- The already-shipped wishlist social sign-in (SFCC-742) redirects to this exact path: `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:333-339` and `:359-365` call `authorizeIDP.mutateAsync({hint, redirectURI: buildRedirectURI(window.location.origin, socialRedirectPath)})` where `socialRedirectPath` comes from `loginConfig.social?.redirectURI` (line 160).

LIKELY IMPACT
Coming back from Apple/Google, `/social-callback?code=...` falls through to the `/:segments+` catch-all at overrides/app/routes.tsx (CategoryPath), so `SocialLoginRedirect` never mounts, `loginIDPUser` is never called, and the shopper is never signed in.

WHAT TO DO
1. First VERIFY the gap is real — do not assume. Confirm the overrides router is the one actually used at runtime (ccExtensibility in package.json:17-20), and confirm nothing else registers the path. Check whether CategoryPath swallows it or 404s.
2. If confirmed, add the three dynamic routes to `overrides/app/routes.tsx`, gated on the same config flags base uses, and placed BEFORE the `/:segments+` catch-all. Mirror base's conditions exactly (enabled && path present).
3. Regenerate the route registry (`node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`) so `.claude/registry/routes.md` reflects the change.
4. Add a test that asserts `/social-callback` resolves to the SocialLoginRedirect component when social login is enabled.

Note: this repo is TypeScript-only inside overrides/. Check AGENTS.md and the audit-tier skill before editing routes.tsx — it is a widely-imported file.
